explanation: Ran EXCLURAD (eta channel, e p -> e' p eta) at W=1.54 GeV, Q2=1.3207 GeV^2, cos(theta*)=0.341379, phi*=36 deg using standard CLAS12 RG-K settings: beam energy 6.53 GeV, vcut=0.166 GeV^2, rc_mode=0 (full O(alpha)). The point passed preflight (well above the eta threshold W~1.486 GeV, cos(theta*) away from the +/-1 poles, inside the lookup-table (W,Q2) coverage). The run completed (exit code 0, 'OK' status) and sigma_Born was computed successfully: 0.0008651649, with the internal Born consistency check (born_check) equal to 1.0, confirming the Born cross section itself is trustworthy. However, delta (the radiative-correction factor sigma_obs/sigma_Born) came out as NaN in both radtot.dat and radcor.dat (both the unpolarized and polarized rows). The stdout integration log shows one of the bremsstrahlung tail integral ('tai:') components for structure-function contribution 3 itself evaluated to NaN, which propagates directly into delta. This is a numerical failure of the O(alpha) radiative tail integration at this specific kinematic point, not an unphysical request -- the point is valid and sigma_Born is reliable, but delta cannot be reported for this run and is set to null.
